records.clean_question:
For five Monday evening shifts, let $x$ be the number of staff and $y$ the number of abusive customers:

| Staff $x$ | 3 | 4 | 2 | 6 | 2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Abusive customers $y$ | 10 | 11 | 13 | 15 | 10 |

a. Fit the least-squares regression line for predicting $y$ from $x$.

b. Predict $y$ when five staff work.

c. Find the sample correlation coefficient.
records.clean_answer: The least-squares line is $\hat y=8.946+0.839x$. For five staff, $\hat y=8.946+0.839(5)=13.143$ abusive customers. The sample correlation is $r=0.6478$, indicating a moderate positive linear association.

records.clean_question:
The ages (years) and second-hand prices (in USD 100) of 11 cars are:

| Age | 5 | 7 | 6 | 6 | 5 | 4 | 7 | 6 | 5 | 5 | 2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Price | 80 | 57 | 58 | 55 | 70 | 88 | 43 | 60 | 69 | 63 | 118 |

Find the sample correlation and interpret it.
records.clean_answer: The sample correlation is $r\approx-0.9570$. This very strong negative linear association means that older cars tend to have lower second-hand prices; correlation alone does not prove causation.
